claims.statement: The 186 held orders are exactly scope EXC-0921: orders allocated under v18 with a split reservation and routed to the east node. 100% of held orders are in EXC-0921 and no order outside EXC-0921 is held.
claims.corroboration: Tier-1 verified exception_audit from Inventory Control (m8_r_exceptions) now corroborates the earlier tier-2 support report (m8_e10): full overlap between held orders and the split-reservation exception cohort.
claims.limitation: m8_r_exceptions itself notes it cannot separate an effect of the rule change from an effect specific to the east-node lanes, since only rule-affected orders were routed there. Correlation/scope match only, not yet a mechanism.

next_action.rationale: We now have an authoritative, discriminating scope (EXC-0921) with 100% overlap to the held orders, but m8_r_exceptions explicitly cannot separate a rule-change effect from an east-node-lane effect (e.g. carrier_feed_lag or dock_capacity). Tracing the cohort's handoffs from allocation through to the carrier for EXC-0921 will show exactly where the process breaks (allocation never releasing the split-reservation exception to the carrier feed, vs. a lag/capacity problem downstream at the carrier or dock), which is the discriminating evidence needed to support or refute the allocation_rule_defect hypothesis versus carrier_feed_lag/dock_capacity before any root_cause claim.
next_action.expected_information_gain: Identifies the specific stage (allocation exception handling vs carrier feed vs dock) where EXC-0921 orders stop progressing, enabling a root_cause claim with discriminating evidence and ruling out at least one competing mechanism_tag.
